author: Dosseman
title: Antakya Children in 2004 67.jpg
description: In 2004 I had a new digital camera, and in Antakya at the time that was a rather flashy object. And not needing to buy expensive film made it possible to take many pictures. In particular children frequently asked to have their picture taken. Often they combined in groups, each kid trying to be as photogenic as possible. This led to a lot of moved images, with a few people in focus, others out of. The better ones I show. Later kids would be surrounded by mobiles, and taking this type of picture became rare.

source_key: commons:File:Cisterna Basílica, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-28, DD 58-60 HDR.jpg
author: Diego Delso
title: Cisterna Basílica, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-28, DD 58-60 HDR.jpg
description: View of the Basilica Cistern , Istanbul , Turkey. The Basilica Cistern, or Cisterna Basilica is the largest of several hundred ancient cisterns that lie beneath the city. This subterranean cistern was called Basilica because it was located under a large public square, the Stoa Basilica, on the First Hill of Constantinople . The cistern, built in the 6th century during the reign of Byzantine emperor Justinian I, provided a water filtration system for the Great Palace of Constantinople and other buildings on the First Hill, and continued to provide water to the Topkapı Palace after the Ottoman conquest in 1453 and into modern times. Today it is kept with little water, for public access inside the space.

author: Diego Delso
title: Mezquita Azul, Estambul, Turquía, 2024-09-30, DD 48-50 HDR.jpg
description: Interior view of the main domes of the Blue Mosque , Istanbul , Turkey. The officially known as Sultan Ahmed Mosque is one of the most iconic and popular monuments of Ottoman architecture. It was constructed between 1609 and 1617 during the rule of Ahmed I and remains a functioning mosque today. It is decorated with thousands of Iznik tiles and painted floral motifs in predominantly blue colours, which give the mosque its popular name. The Blue Mosque, included in the UNESCO World Heritage Site list in 1985, was built next to the former Hippodrome and stands across from the Hagia Sophia, another popular tourist site.
categories: Ceiling of the Sultan Ahmed I Mosque
